key_insight: Jointly optimizing a probabilistic belief over user intent and the assistance policy end-to-end (BRACE) yields more adaptive, context-aware shared-autonomy than decoupled or statically blended approaches, improving task success while respecting user agency.
problem_solved: Overcomes suboptimal goal inference and fixed assistance arbitration in shared autonomy by fusing belief estimation and policy learning so assistance adapts to uncertain intent and unstructured environments.
method: Formulate shared autonomy as a POMDP-like problem where a Bayesian belief over user goals is maintained and updated from observations.
Encode context (environment and user cues) with a learned context encoder and feed the belief + context into a reinforcement-learning policy.
Train belief update and assistance policy end-to-end (BRACE) with an objective that balances task performance and user agency, replacing static blending or separate modules.
impact: Makes shared-autonomy systems more robust and practical: less manual tuning, better performance in real-world/uncertain settings, and smoother, agency-preserving assistance—useful for HRI, assistive robotics, and adaptive interfaces.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: sensors → context encoder → Bayesian belief over goals → RL assistance policy → robot action
Side-by-side bar chart: BRACE vs static blending / decoupled baselines on success rate, intervention frequency, and user override rate
Graphical model / POMDP sketch showing latent user intent, observations, and actions with belief updates
Tradeoff curve icon: task success vs. user agency (showing BRACE nearer the Pareto frontier)
paper_title: End-to-end Optimization of Belief and Policy Learning in Shared Autonomy Paradigms
paper_authors: MH Farhadi, Ali Rabiee, Sima Ghafoori, Anna Cetera, Andrew Fisher
